rule: A direct write is a write-method use whose receiver is the raw `ctx.context.adapter` expression, or an alias bound to it (assignment or parameter default, declared per file below), or a helper parameter that a pinned anchor call site receives `ctx.context.adapter` through. Scope is exactly the files declared below — the fixed composition this plan mounts (core db/api/oauth2 layers, the organization plugin, @better-auth/sso, @better-auth/scim, @better-auth/core). Other plugin directories bundled inside better-auth are not mounted by this composition and are out of scope by declaration; mounting a new plugin is a reviewed scope change to this manifest. Every structural use in scope must appear here; a package upgrade that changes versions, line numbers, snippets or the set of uses fails the scan (scripts/check-better-auth-adapter-writes.mjs).

better-auth:dist/db/internal-adapter.mjs.adapter: createInternalAdapter(adapter, ctx) receives ctx.context.adapter; raw parameter uses below bypass the ALS store

writes.disposition: invite-member native resend branch rewrites expiresAt; invitation.resend is an OpenBot controlled cancel+create command, and the native resend branch is unreachable through the ingress
dynamic role create; dynamicAccessControl is off and every role endpoint is X in interfaces §3.2
dynamic role delete; dynamicAccessControl is off and every role endpoint is X in interfaces §3.2
dynamic role update; dynamicAccessControl is off and every role endpoint is X in interfaces §3.2
assignOrganization writes a member row; organizationProvisioning.disabled:true is a hard precondition, so the callback cannot reach this branch
register writes an ssoProvider row; the controlled config write goes through ingress → auth.api inside the executor transaction and rejects a client-supplied organizationId

managed SCIM bearer-token verification hands the raw adapter method to a database object; SCIM writes are translated by the ingress to auth.api inside the executor transaction and the native handler is never mounted for writes

reserveVerificationValue writes the verification reservation on the base adapter; only the recovery ingress reaches it, through auth.api inside the identity transaction, so the reservation lands in the outer tx and a failure rolls the command back
reserveVerificationValue re-reads the reservation on the base adapter to make a duplicate portable; part of the same unclassified-adapter flow as line 893

verify-domain hands the raw base adapter to completeDomainVerification as a parameter; the incrementOne on ssoProvider bypasses the ALS store and would land on a pool connection even inside an executor transaction. Not in interfaces §3.1's original table; found by the T01.03 audit and added here so the fixed build's bypass set is complete. The /sso/verify-domain controlled config write is owned by the SSO task (P12) and the mount audit (P23): until it is translated through ingress → auth.api or closed, this pin keeps the bypass visible instead of silently reclassified.
